image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a metallic green tiger beetle on a sandy, textured ground. The beetle exhibits iridescent elytra with distinct pale cream-colored markings. Its head is broad with large compound eyes and visible mandibles. Long, filiform antennae extend backward. Six slender legs are visible, gripping the substrate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head broader than pronotum with large prominent compound eyes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible in profile, appearing wider than the neck region (pronotum), and the large, dark compound eye is a dominant feature.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long sickle-shaped mandibles adapted for capturing prey.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Prominent, curved mandibles are visible extending from the front of the head, consistent with predatory beetle anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Filiform antennae extending well beyond the midbody.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two long, thread-like antennae are visible sweeping back along the body, exceeding the length of the thorax.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated, slender body with distinctly narrow proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall silhouette is elongated and streamlined, typical of cursorial beetles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bright metallic coloration in green, bronze, or copper tones.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The exoskeleton displays a vibrant, iridescent metallic green hue with highlights suggesting a hard, shiny surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive pale markings on smooth iridescent elytra.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Cream/white irregular spots are clearly visible on the wing covers (elytra), matching the species' pattern.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Six slender cursorial legs enabling rapid pursuit.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Three legs are clearly visible on the near side; the positioning and partial visibility of the far side legs imply a standard hexapod structure without obvious extra or missing limbs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (head, thorax, abdomen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The segmentation between head, pronotum (thorax shield), and elytra (covering abdomen) is distinct and anatomically correct.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The sand texture shows slight smearing and lack of fine granular detail immediately around the contact points of the tarsi, suggesting minor generation softness or edge blending issues.
The very ends of the antennae fade into blur slightly more aggressively than natural depth-of-field might dictate, though this is minor.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic identity and rule out generic beetle hallucinations.
To verify that the thin, complex structures (legs/antennae) are topologically connected to the body and not floating or fused with the background.
To assess the realism of the metallic reflections and the coherence of the lighting/shadows on the exoskeleton.
To ensure the beetle sits correctly on the plane of the sand without geometric sinking or floating artifacts.

focus_areas: Integrity of leg attachments (no fusion with body or ground)
Continuity of antennae (no breaking or fading into nothingness)
Realism of metallic specular highlights on elytra
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the connection points of the legs. AI often struggles with thin limbs on textured backgrounds. Verify if the 'pale markings' on the elytra look like painted-on textures or integrated structural coloration. Check if the mandibles have a valid 3D volume or appear flat.
